label: Town of St. Albans
header:
# Town of St. Albans municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 22; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 150 (Town of St. Albans): sec. 2 provides that the town's officers are governed by general law

Town of St. Albans official website, Selectboard page (October 2026): Jack Brigham, Chair (term expires 2028); Bryan DesLauriers, Vice Chair (expires 2027); Jeff Sanders (expires 2028); Cathy Montagne (expires 2029); Chelsea Mulheron (expires 2027). Mulheron holds the seat the FY 2025 Town Report gives to Amanda Headley on a two-year term to 2027, with the same 2027 expiry -- a vacancy appointment under 24 V.S.A. sec. 963, so she is seated APPOINTED and Headley is not seated

Town of St. Albans, official ballot for the Annual Town Meeting of March 3, 2026 with the hand-tallied results, attested by Town Clerk Anna Bourdon (830 total votes): John 'Jack' Brigham was elected to the two-year seat with 692 votes and Cathy Montagne to the three-year seat with 734 votes

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): names Jack Brigham (Chair), Amanda Headley (Vice Chair), Bryan Deslauriers, Cathy Montagne, and Jeff Sanders; the town's own current Selectboard page governs over the directory for the fifth seat (see the Mulheron note)

Town of St. Albans, official ballot for the Annual Town Meeting of March 3, 2026 with the hand-tallied results, attested by Town Clerk Anna Bourdon (830 total votes): the Town Constable contest was write-in only, with no printed candidate and no total published, so the seat stands unfilled here (Hatfield is seated as a justice of the peace below)

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen St. Albans Town justices of the peace: John 'Jack' Brigham, Tina Brosky, Bruce Cheeseman, Bryan Deslauriers, Stanley Dukas, Jonathan Giroux, Peter Hatfield, Diane Lareau, Roger Luneau, John McCarthy, Pamela McCarthy, David McWilliams, Joseph Montcalm, Gerald Morong, and Albin Voegele (the town's block in the listing continues across a page break)
Town of St. Albans official website, Board of Civil Authority page: states the board 'consists of 15 Justices of the Peace' and names fourteen of them (all but Bryan Deslauriers)

jp_election.name: Town of St. Albans Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): the certified listing names fifteen winners for St. Albans Town's fifteen justice of the peace seats. Bryan Deslauriers is among the certified winners but the town's Board of Civil Authority page, which states the board consists of 15 justices, names only the other fourteen and omits him, although he remains Selectboard Vice Chair; he is held as a departed winner and no person record, candidacy, or winner entry is created for his justice seat (the election's vote_for stays at the fifteen-seat slate size)
Town of St. Albans official website, Board of Civil Authority page: names the fourteen serving justices of the peace
